Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice H.S.Grewal
Present:- | Mr. Vinod Ghai, Senior Advocate with

Mr. Arnav Ghai, Advocate,
Ms. Kashish Sahni, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Kumar Jangra, A.A.G, Haryana.
Mr. Amandeep Singh Manaise, Advocate for the complainant.

3K 2k
H.S. Grewal, J.(Oral)
1.

The present petition has been filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 seeking regular bail in case FIR No.271 dated 18.09.2025, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B IPC, registered at Police Station Udyog Vihar, Gurugram.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the petitioner is alleged to have furnished a forged/fake high value bank guarantee to the complainant company for procuring wheat supply.
3. Learned Senior counsel for the petitioner, however, submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case and the FIR has been lodged after an inordinate delay of two months.

He has also referred to the | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document Chandigarh AMIT KAUNDAL 2026.02.05 15:09 2026: PHHC-017 108  CRM-M-3144-2026 on?
Rajendera Cherukuri
Alias Cherukuri

... vs State Of Haryana on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89852841/
1 e
-mail at Annexure P-2
which reveals that the matter between the parties has already settled and an amount of Rs.70 lakhs was paid to the complainant- Company.
Learned counsel further submits that the petitioner has already cleared dues and 'No Objection Certificate' in this regard has already been issued.
It is also submitted that the entire transactional amount was settled.
It is also submitted that the petitioner is in custody for the last more than 03 months.
He, therefore, prays for release of the petitioner on regular bail as the trial is likely to take a long time.
4. Learned State counsel vehemently opposes the prayer for grant of regular bail to the petitioner.
Learned State counsel has filed the custody certificate in Court, which is taken on record.
As per the custody certificate, the petitioner is in custody for the last more than 03 months and 08 days.

He,
upon instructions, submits that although challan has been presented but charges are yet to be framed.
5. Learned counsel for the complainant has put in appearance and has filed the Power of Attorney in Court which is taken on record.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. In view of the above submissions of learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the fact that the petitioner is in custody for the last more than 03 months and 08 days and that the trial is likely to take a long time, this Court deems it fit to grant the concession of regular bail to the petitioner during the pendency of the trial as the continuous detention of the petitioner would not serve the ends of justice.
| attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document Chandigarh 2026: PHHC-017 108  CRM-M-3144-2026 eg 8.
Therefore, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail on his furnishing requisite bail bonds, surety bonds to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court/Duty Magistrate/Chief Judicial Magistrate concemed.
9. However, it is made clear that in case the petitioner misuses the concession of bail, the State would be at liberty to seek cancellation of his bail.
